# Project facts

What the Sprecher East website runs on and how to work with it locally: stack, hosting,
environment variables, and known gotchas. It describes the system; the rules for changing it
are in [`AGENTS.md`](/AGENTS.md), and where code goes is in [`architecture/`](/docs/architecture/README.md).
Keep it current: a change that makes a line here wrong updates it in the same PR.

## Project Overview

Grassroots neighborhood website for Sprecher East (Madison, WI), live at https://sprechereast.com.
It is an unofficial, AI-assisted initiative (ground rules in [`AGENTS.md`](/AGENTS.md#ground-rules)).

**Repos:**

- Website (this repo, PUBLIC): `boulaajaj/sprecher-east-neighborhood-website`
- Strategy docs: `boulaajaj/sprecher-east-strategy` (PRIVATE, archived and read-only since #538; this repo is the source of truth)

## Current Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 (App Router, TypeScript; Turbopack builds), React 19.2
- **CSS**: Tailwind CSS v4. Design tokens: the contract in `src/platform/theme/tokens.ts`, values in `src/themes/default/theme.css`, Tailwind mapping in `src/platform/theme/tailwind.css` (#146)
- **CMS**: Payload CMS v3 Website Template at `/admin` (self-hosted, SQLite `data/payload.db`). Editors can schedule a page, post or event to publish or unpublish: Payload's jobs queue runs it inside the app every minute (`jobs.autoRun`), and pages re-render at most every 10 minutes, so visitors see it within 10 minutes (decision 0011, #141)
- **Auth**: Payload native auth (Users collection with `auth: true`); roles `admin`, `editor`, `guest` (the default for new accounts), `resident` (a verified neighbour) and `agent` (#336, #520); the first account on an empty database is an `admin` (#354). Pages and server actions ask `src/modules/accounts/` who is signed in (`getCurrentUser`, `requireUser`, `requireRole`); sign-in (Payload's `login` helper from `@payloadcms/next/auth`), sign-out, password changes and forgot/reset password (Payload's `forgotPassword` and `resetPassword`, with a branded email linking to `/reset-password`, #269) are its server actions. Forgot password runs only from the site's page, behind the robot check and per-connection and site-wide limits, and Payload sends the email after the answer, so the time doesn't show whether an account exists (#282); Payload's REST and GraphQL forgot password answer 403, and `/admin/forgot` redirects to `/forgot-password`. Neighbours sign up on `/sign-up` (as guests) (linked from the header, the mobile menu and `/login` (#296), and offered on `/confirm-email` after a contact sender confirms) through Payload's `create` with `auth.verify`: the branded verification email links to `/verify-account`, and an unverified account can't sign in or get a reset email (#187). Verifying takes the Confirm button and the robot check on that page; Payload's REST verify answers 403, its GraphQL verify mutation is refused, and `/admin/users/verify/<token>` redirects to `/verify-account` (#303). Signing up again with an unverified account's email sends a new link, at most 3 times per 3 hours, counted on the account; a resent link asks the person to choose the password on `/verify-account` before the account opens, so a password from an earlier sign-up never activates (#289). A confirmation or verification link opened again after it was used says the email or account is already confirmed, with no Confirm button: both pages read the link's state when they open, changing nothing (#391). A sign-in lasts two hours (Payload's default `tokenExpiration`); ticking "Keep me signed in" on `/login` makes it last 7 days, then the person signs in again (#587)
- **Email**: `@payloadcms/email-nodemailer` over SMTP (Mailgun in production); logs to the console when `SMTP_HOST` is unset. Email addresses typed into public forms are confirmed by link (`src/modules/verification/`, #183): the link opens a page whose Confirm button also passes the robot check, so mail scanners that open the link confirm nothing (#303); a contact message's emails go out only once its sender confirms (#287). Unconfirmed messages and addresses are deleted after 48 hours, and a confirmed sender's contact data 12 months after their last message, by hourly tasks in Payload's jobs queue that run inside the app (`jobs.autoRun`, decision 0010)
- **Spam protection**: Cloudflare Turnstile on public forms and on the Confirm buttons of `/confirm-email` and `/verify-account`, plus size and rate limits (decision records in `docs/architecture/decisions/`)
- **Tests**: Vitest unit tests next to the code (`*.test.ts`, and `*.test.mjs` for the Claude Code hooks in `.claude/hooks/`, #446, and the scripts in `scripts/`, #144), run with `npm test` and in CI (#139). Component tests (`*.test.tsx`) run in jsdom with Testing Library and axe (`expectAccessible` in `src/platform/ui/testing/`). A few tests send real REST and Local API requests to Payload booted on in-memory SQLite (`src/payload.config.protectedFields.test.ts`, #299). End-to-end tests (`e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright, #311) walk each account and contact flow on a phone and a desktop, with axe on each step, and `e2e/alignment.spec.ts` (#678) measures a seeded post of awkward cards at six widths and fails if matching parts of cards in a row aren't on one line, or if the legend under a captioned image starts above its caption or isn't as wide as the image (#658): `npx playwright test` starts `e2e/serve.mjs` (a fresh SQLite database, a production build, a local SMTP catcher the tests read links from, no Turnstile keys) and CI runs it as `End-to-end tests` (not required yet). Where `next build` can't reach Google Fonts, `E2E_DEV=1` runs them against `next dev` instead. The run's build replaces `.next`, so build again before a local `npm start`
- **Unused code**: knip (`npm run knip`, config in `knip.jsonc`) finds files, exports and packages nothing uses; CI runs it on every PR (`Unused code (knip)`, not required yet, #445). A module's entry files are its contract, so their exports aren't reported
- **Duplicate code**: jscpd 4.3.0 (`npm run duplication`, config and ignore list in `.jscpd.json`) fails on a repeated block of 12 lines or more (and at least 30 tokens, so a run of blank or one-word lines isn't counted) in `src`, `intelligence`, `ops` (shell scripts too) and `scripts` (tests, migrations, seed, generated files, the gallery and `src/app/(payload)/`, which Payload generates and rewrites, are ignored; the last clones came down in #622, under #614); CI runs it on every PR (`Duplicate code (jscpd)`, not required yet, #611). The pure-JavaScript 4.x line is used on purpose, not 5.x, which is a prebuilt Rust binary
- **Generated reference** (#714): `npm run docs:generate` loads the Payload config (no database, no server; `tsx` resolves the `@payload-config` alias) and writes one page per collection and global to `docs/reference/content-types/`: fields, access per operation, hooks by phase, drafts, with the file each function lives in. `npm run docs:check` regenerates in memory and fails on any difference; CI runs it as `Knowledge sync` (required). Never edit those pages by hand. The code is in `scripts/generate-reference.mjs`, `scripts/content-types/` and `scripts/reference/`
- **Rich Text**: Lexical editor with slash menu, toolbars, inline images, and custom blocks
- **Icons**: Lucide React
- **Payload docs for agents**: https://payloadcms.com/llms-full.txt (the whole Payload documentation in one file)
- **Hosting**: Hostinger VPS (Ubuntu 24.04, PM2 + Caddy)

  domain sends HSTS (`max-age` in `ops/caddy/hsts.caddy`, rolled out in stages; no
  `includeSubDomains` or `preload`), and plain HTTP to the IP on port 80 redirects to
  `https://sprechereast.com` with a 308 (`ops/caddy-https.sh`, #235)

## Architecture

**Read [`docs/architecture/`](/docs/architecture/README.md) before writing code.** It has the
target structure (one module per business area under `src/modules/`, shared code in
`src/platform/`, routes and composition only in `src/app/`), the dependency rules, where each kind
of code goes, naming [conventions](/docs/architecture/conventions.md), the [glossary](/docs/architecture/glossary.md),
the [data model](/docs/architecture/data-model.md) and [decision records](/docs/architecture/decisions/README.md).

Every business area has moved to that structure (#127), and lint fails on an import that breaks
its rules (#137). The Payload website template's folders are gone; the few exceptions (seed,
generated files) are listed in [`architecture/`](/docs/architecture/README.md#exceptions).

```
src/
  app/                 Next.js App Router: routes and composition only
    (frontend)/        Public routes (home, posts, events, faq, resources, search, login, account)
    (payload)/         Payload admin and API routes (generated; leave alone)
  modules/             One folder per business area
    accounts/          Who is signed in, sign-in and password flows, the users collection
    agents/            Agent access over MCP and the agents' run history
    contact/           Form safeguards, the form block
    directory/         FAQ, local resources, team members
    events/            Events and the upcoming rule
    news/              Posts, categories, search
    site/              CMS pages, page-builder blocks, heroes, header, footer, redirects, link groups
  platform/            Shared by every module; imports no module
    email/             SMTP settings for password-reset and form emails
    lib/               Pure helpers: paging, roles, dates and the site timezone, URLs, `cn`
    payload/           Role checks, access functions, media collection, link field, default editor, publishedAt hook, admin components
    richtext/          The `RichText` renderer, the blocks inside rich text, plain-text conversion
    seo/               Page metadata and Open Graph helpers
    theme/             The theme contract (`tokens.ts`), its Tailwind mapping, theme options and decorations, light and dark mode providers
    turnstile/         The robot check (Cloudflare Turnstile): widget and server verifier
    ui/                The UI kit: `Button`, `Link`, `Media`, `LinkButton`, `JsonLd`, `Breadcrumbs`, `LoadMore`…
  endpoints/seed/      Seed data and script (exception)
  migrations/          Database migrations (generated)
  payload.config.ts    CMS composition: collections, globals, plugins
  proxy.ts             Next.js proxy (middleware)
```

## Design Tokens

Colors, radius and dark-mode values are tokens: named in `src/platform/theme/tokens.ts`, valued in
`src/themes/default/theme.css`, and checked against the contract and WCAG AA by
`src/platform/theme/themes.test.ts` (decisions 0006 and 0012). The table of
light and dark values is in [`guidelines/nextjs-tailwind.md`](/docs/guidelines/nextjs-tailwind.md#design-tokens).

## Local Dev Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # fill in secrets (see Env Vars below)
npm run dev                         # → http://localhost:3000
# Visit /admin for first-time Payload admin setup (the first account created there is the admin)
```

## Env Vars (all secrets go in `.env.local`, never commit)

| Var                                                                                       | Purpose                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PAYLOAD_SECRET`                                                                          | Payload JWT signing (32+ random chars)                           |
| `DATABASE_URI`                                                                            | `file:./data/payload.db`                                         |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`                                                                  | `http://localhost:3000` (dev) or production URL                  |
| `PREVIEW_SECRET`                                                                          | Draft preview URL signing                                        |
| `SITE_TIMEZONE`                                                                           | IANA timezone for dates (default: `America/Chicago`)             |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`                                  | Robot check on public forms; set both or neither, then rebuild   |
| `TURNSTILE_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES`                                                             | Extra hostnames a Turnstile token may come from (optional)       |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_FROM_NAME` | Outgoing email; unset `SMTP_HOST` logs emails instead            |
| `CONTACT_NOTIFY_EMAIL`, `CONTACT_EMAIL_FROM`                                              | Used by the seed only, for the contact form's owner notification |
| `SEED_PASSWORD`                                                                           | Seed only: the demo user's password (random when unset)          |

| Var | Purpose |
|-----|---------|

## Known Gotchas

- **Row counts of lists in rich-text blocks** (#664): Payload's own array validator reads a number as the row count, and Admin's form state sends a list as its count (a half-built row holds only its `id`), so `entries: 2` passes `minRows: 2` and is stored as an empty list, and a native check leaves "at least 2 Rows" on screen after a row is added. The Timeline, Key facts and Fact tabs lists count their own rows (`rowsBetween` in `src/platform/richtext/editorial/rowCount.ts`): judged under `event: 'onChange'` too (Admin sends the rows or their count, so the reason shows under the field and clears when the last needed row is added; a value that can't be counted gets no opinion), and on the real save a number counts as no rows; never throws. `minRows` and `maxRows` stay on the field for the Add button
- **`admin` key on nested lists**: an array or blocks field inside a rich-text block gets no `admin` object from Payload, and one without an `admin` key crashes Payload's `isRowCollapsed` (`initCollapsed`) when saving. Give every array and blocks field in such a block an `admin` key (`factTabsBlockConfig.test.ts` and `chartBlockConfig.test.ts` check it)
- **npm installs**: Always use `--legacy-peer-deps` for Payload packages
- **Payload REST route**: `REST_GET(config)` — curried, NOT `REST_GET(req, config)`
- **Payload importMap**: Auto-generated on dev server start at `src/app/(payload)/admin/importMap.js`
- **`defaultSort`**: Must be on collection root, NOT inside `admin: {}`
- **`npx payload run` broken on Node v24**: Use direct node scripts instead
- **`graphql` package**: Must install separately from `@payloadcms/graphql`
- **`overrideAccess`**: Set it on every Local API call: `false` for what a visitor may see, `true` only where access must be bypassed, with a comment saying why. The seed's writes don't set it yet, and the header and footer are read with `overrideAccess: true` (#251)
- **`server-only`**: Server code outside the CMS config that queries Payload or reads cookies (utilities, `data/`, `use-cases/`, `server.ts`) starts with `import 'server-only'`, so a client component importing it fails the build. Collections, hooks and plugins never import it: the Payload CLI (`migrate`, seed) loads them outside Next.js, where it throws. Hooks use the `req.payload` they are given
- **Cache tags**: Expire them with `expireCacheTag()` from `src/platform/payload/expireCacheTag.ts`. Since Next 16, `revalidateTag` needs a second argument; the helper passes `{ expire: 0 }`, so the next visitor gets fresh content
- **`next build` skips the type check**: `next.config.js` sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`, because CI's required Type-check step already checks types and the step timed out the deploy on the server (#246). CI runs `npx next typegen` before `npx tsc --noEmit`, so the route types in `.next/types` (page, layout and route handler exports) are checked too (#248). Run both locally; a green build alone doesn't mean the types are right
- **The release is built without content**: the deploy builds in CI against an empty database, so the server drops the prerendered pages before the switch and each page renders from the live database on its first visit (#245). `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values come from the server's `.env.local` at build time; after changing one there, redeploy (Actions → Deploy to VPS → Run workflow)
- **Agents and MCP** (#336): agents use `/api/mcp` (Payload's MCP plugin) with an API key an admin creates in Admin (Agents → API Keys) for an `agent` account; the key is shown once and never goes in the repo or an issue. Runs are under Agents → Agent Runs. The plugin imports `typescript` at runtime, so `typescript` is a production dependency (the release prunes dev ones), and `package.json` overrides its `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` to patched versions; drop those overrides once the plugin ships them
- **Proxy**: `src/proxy.ts` (Next 16's name for middleware) answers 404 for junk paging URLs and malformed event category filters before they render (#119), and sends `/events?category=<slug>` to `/events/category/<slug>` (#122, decision 0015)
- **Upload URLs stay relative**: `getMediaUrl()` turns Payload's upload URLs (prefixed with `serverURL`) back into `/api/media/file/...`, so next/image treats them as local; since Next 16 it refuses remote URLs on private IPs such as localhost
- **Sign-in cookie is Secure in production**: the Users collection sets `auth.cookies.secure` when `NODE_ENV` is `production` (#234), so signing in (site and `/admin`) works over HTTPS only. Over plain http the browser drops the cookie; the IP on port 80 redirects to HTTPS (#235). `next dev` on `http://localhost` is unaffected
- **"Keep me signed in" is our code, not a Payload setting** (#587): `auth.tokenExpiration` is one value per collection and sets the token, the stored session and the cookie together, with no per-sign-in override in 3.91. When the box is ticked, `data/rememberedSession.ts` signs the token again for 7 days (`REMEMBER_ME_LIFETIME_MS`), extends that session's `expiresAt` with one `UPDATE` of its own row in `users_sessions` (never a write-back of the whole `sessions` list, which could undo a sign-out or lose a new sign-in; Payload deletes sessions past it at the account's next sign-in anywhere, which would end the remembered one early) and sets the cookie for 7 days. A Payload upgrade that changes sessions or `jwtSign` shows up in `rememberedSession.payload.test.ts`, which runs real Payload. `/admin`'s own sign-in form stays at two hours
- **Open the site at exactly `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`** (#281): Payload's `csrf` list is that one address, and it ignores the sign-in cookie on a request whose `Origin` isn't in it. Server actions always send `Origin`, so on `http://127.0.0.1:3000` with the URL set to `http://localhost:3000` you can sign in and load `/account`, yet the header keeps saying "Log In" (even after a reload), and changing the password says you're signed out. Use the same host and port. Don't add origins to `csrf` to hide it
- **Live Preview**: posts and events (#363) open their real page from the draft in Admin's Live Preview, refreshed on autosave by `LivePreviewListener` (`RefreshRouteOnSave`). A card preview is never shown inside a post or event page's layout (#532)
- **Draft Preview**: Requires `PREVIEW_SECRET` env var for signed preview URLs
- **Timezone**: Configured via `SITE_TIMEZONE` env var (default: `America/Chicago`). Use `startOfToday()` and `SITE_TIMEZONE` from `src/platform/lib/timezone.ts`. Never hardcode timezone strings or use bare `new Date().setHours(0,0,0,0)`. Day-only dates (midnight UTC) must be formatted with `timeZone: 'UTC'` to avoid off-by-one; `formatDateTime()` handles this automatically.
